Project Title: Aarthi — Tamil AI Receptionist for Small Clinics
Tech Stack: STT: Custom / Other, LLM: Google Gemini, TTS: Custom / Other
Project Description:
A Tamil-speaking AI receptionist that answers a clinic's phone line and books,
reschedules or cancels appointments against a live calendar. It also calls
patients back automatically within seconds of them submitting the clinic's web
enquiry form — handling Tamil, Tanglish and English with no menus and no key presses.
[ cut-off human in repitaion , give back their time to interact who already in clinic and other important human needed works]
Solution / Problem Solved:
WHAT AARTHI DOES

1. Answers real phone calls in Tamil
Speaks Tanglish — Tamil sentences with business words kept in English
(doctor, appointment, book, date, time). No IVR menus, no key presses.
Switches to English automatically if the caller speaks English.

2.Routes symptoms to the right doctor
The patient describes the problem in their own words. Aarthi maps it to the
correct department and names the doctor — skin to Dermatology, teeth to Dental,
everything else to General. The caller never has to know the department.

3.Books against a live calendar
She checks real availability before offering any time, and offers only slots
that are genuinely free. She refuses Sundays, the 1-3 PM lunch break, and past
dates. Two patients can never take the same slot.

4.Recognises returning callers
On the second call she identifies the patient by their phone number and opens
with their existing appointment — "ஓ Ragul! உங்களுக்கு Monday 4:30 PM-க்கு
appointment book ஆயிருக்கு" — without asking who they are.

5.Rescues cancellations
When a patient cancels, she immediately asks whether the timing was the problem
and offers the next free slot, carrying over their details so they don't repeat
themselves. A lost appointment becomes a rebooked one.

6.Books for family and friends
"என் பிரண்டுக்கு பண்ணனும்" — she takes the other person's name and books it
under theirs.

7.Understands natural speech
"ok பண்ணிடுங்க", "சரி", "பண்ணுங்க" — anything that means go ahead is accepted.
She never instructs the caller to say yes or no.

8.Calls web leads back automatically
A patient fills the clinic's enquiry form and their phone rings within five
seconds. No staff involvement, no queue, no callback list.

9.Sends the location on WhatsApp
Asked for directions, she says the area out loud and WhatsApps the map link.

Notifies the clinic by email
Every booking reaches the clinic owner's inbox. Patients get WhatsApp, staff get
email — each channel goes to whoever actually uses it.

10.Records and transcribes every call
Full audio plus a written transcript of both sides.

11.Never invents anything
She will not claim an appointment is booked unless the booking actually
succeeded, will not name a doctor who does not exist, and will not quote a fee
she does not know — she says the staff will confirm it. Every claim she makes is
backed by a real system result.

12.Detects medical emergencies and stops booking
Chest pain, breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, fainting, seizures, accidents,
stroke signs, poisoning, labour pain, an unresponsive baby, or anyone at risk of
self-harm — Aarthi stops the booking conversation immediately. She does not offer
a slot, does not quote clinic hours, and does not tell them to wait. She tells
them to go to the nearest hospital or call 108, and offers to transfer the call
to clinic staff straight away. A same-day appointment is not an answer to chest
pain, and the agent is built to know that.

13.Hands over to a real human
When a caller is in an emergency or is distressed and needs a person, Aarthi
transfers the live call to clinic staff — the caller stays on the line and a human
picks up. She also refuses to give medical advice of any kind: she will not name a
medicine, give a dose, or judge whether a symptom is serious. That is the doctor's
job, and she says so.

14.Appointments appear in the clinic calendar
Every booking made on a call lands in the clinic's calendar in real time, visible
to staff with the patient's name, date and time. Cancellations and reschedules
update it immediately, which is what keeps double-booking impossible.

Project Title: Araxys: A Voice Native Freight Forwarding Desk
Tech Stack: STT: Custom / Other, LLM: Custom / Other, TTS: Custom / Other, Squad Hotlines: ARUN (): +917965854267
Project Description:
Araxys is a voice run freight forwarding desk. Two AI agents answer the hotline in Tamil and English, quote from a live rate card, verify real container space in three dimensions, and close a booking before the call ends.

Everything spoken on the phone flows directly into a CRM. The system allocates the cargo to a sailing, and generates all twelve shipping documents without anyone re typing a single field.
Solution / Problem Solved:
A freight forwarder's front desk is a phone, and it leaks. Customers ring at all hours, describe their cargo in whatever language they think in, and ask what it costs. Unless a human happens to be free, that enquiry is gone. What does get answered lands in a notepad, and somebody re enters it into three separate systems hours later.

Priya handles the commercial call. She works out the route and checks whether the cargo physically fits an available container. That means every axis aligned orientation, stackability, payload limits, and how much container floor length the cargo actually consumes. It is not a naive volume comparison, the kind that claims 30 CBM fits inside a 33 CBM box, or misses that a 2.6m crate will never enter a 20GP with 2.39m of interior height. She quotes from a published rate card, negotiates within a defined band, and fixes a sailing date.

Arun takes the warm handoff. As the documentation desk, he collects the shipper, consignee, HS code, and package detail that a commercial invoice legally requires. The customer never repeats a single detail they already gave Priya.

Voice is what makes it work, because this industry runs on calls, not forms. The agents speak Tamil and English, including mid sentence code switching, and they remember which language each caller used. A customer who spoke Tamil last time is greeted in Tamil next time. They ask one question at a time and then wait. The shopping list question, where an agent fires four requests in one breath, is what makes most voice agents unusable on a real phone line.

The agents make no tool calls mid conversation. This is deliberate. A lookup during a live call is latency the customer hears as dead air. Instead, the moment a call ends, the transcript is parsed into 39 structured fields, the record is promoted to a booking, container space is allocated, and the agents' entire knowledge base is republished. The next call opens with an agent that already knows.

Project Title: Aaradhya: AI-Powered Voice Automation for Jewellery Retail Customer Engagement
Tech Stack: STT: Sarvam AI, LLM: OpenAI (GPT-4o), TTS: Cartesia
Project Description:
Aaradhya is a single multilingual voice AI agent for gold and jewellery showrooms that answers inbound calls about live gold rates, savings schemes and general store questions, and makes outbound calls to remind existing scheme members about due installments and to share festive offers. It detects the caller's intent from their own words, pulls the rate from a live source, and turns buying or 
scheme enrolment interest into a scored lead with a callback slot for the sales team.
Solution / Problem Solved:
Jewellery showrooms often juggle three very different call needs with the same limited staff: 
1. New customers asking about rates/schemes - need to become leads.
2. Scheme members needing payment reminders, missed ones cause defaults.
3. General callers asking about festive offers and collections.

Staff can't keep up, so leads go cold and reminders get skipped.

Aaradhya handles all three on one number, detects intent, pulls live 
gold rates (never hardcoded), explains schemes, captures leads, sends 
reminders, and shares offers.
                                                                                                                                                                                    
Voice is the right medium here  because gold buying is a trust-sensitive, high-value decision, customers want to hear a confirmed answer, not read one and a large share of jewellery buyers, particularly older and less tech comfortable customers, are simply more at ease speaking than typing into an app or chatbot.
